keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The pages give the city's size (2 km2 Formative, 5 km2 Classic, 10 km2 Postclassic), never its territory; a 25 km radius is the researcher's reading of 'regional center'. Whether Classic Cholula was Teotihuacan's dependency is not said on any page opened (re-read: the Cholula page says only that it 'seems to have avoided, at least partially, that city's fate of violent destruction' and that the Great Pyramid's early stages 'show stylistic resemblance to early Teotihuacan'; the Teotihuacan page: 'competed to fill the power void'). The overlap with Cliopatria's Teotihuacan shapes (5 of Cholula's 7 cells) is resolved in the teotihuacan dossier, whose shapes are now a 40 km circle around the city with no cell shared with this one. Ends in 649 (review fix): from 650 the 25 km circle contains Cacaxtla's capital cell, the core of another state ('Cacaxtla and Xochitecatl prospered 650–900 CE'); see cholula_650.

correction.text: Cholula and its hinterland without the Cacaxtla-Xochitécatl core: 'Cacaxtla and Xochitecatl prospered 650–900 CE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix). Cholula's 25 km circle (7 cells) contains cell 295354, Cacaxtla's capital and one of the 2 cells of its 10 km core; subtracting that core leaves 6 cells, the city of Cholula included. The Cacaxtla page dates the rise of the twin centres to 650-900 CE and the fall of Cholula to c. 650-750 ('After the fall of the nearby city Cholula (c. 650 – 750)'); the wider 30 km hegemony comes off in cholula_750. Ledger: the 650 loss.

correction.text: the city of Cholula and its southern hinterland only, while Cacaxtla was 'the hegemonic power in this part of the Tlaxcala–Puebla valley'; the city itself (10 km) stays Cholula's as the Olmeca-Xicallanca capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after 'the fall of the nearby city Cholula (c. 650 – 750)' (Cacaxtla page) the northern valley is Cacaxtla's; Cholula itself remained occupied as the Olmeca-Xicallanca capital (Cholula page, Tlachihualtepetl phase 700–1200). Corrected in the repair (found while fixing 650..749, not in the review): the first version (Cholula 25 km minus Cacaxtla 30 km) left the city's own cell outside the shape for 750-900, because Cacaxtla's 30 km disk reaches Cholula (about 20 km away), although the Cholula page makes the city the Olmeca-Xicallanca capital (Tlachihualtepetl phase 700-1200); the 10 km city circle (1 cell) is added back, giving 4 cells. The Cacaxtla page also says 'Warriors from Cacaxtla appear to have taken over Cholula for a time, but they were ultimately expelled by the Toltecs' (undated), which this shape does not draw.

correction.text: Cholula and the Puebla valley again after Cacaxtla's end c. 900; Postclassic Cholula 'covered 10 square kilometers and had a population of thirty to fifty thousand'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. From 1200 Cholula was subject to others (Tolteca-Chichimeca 1200, Tlaxcala 'sometime between 1200 and 1517', the Aztecs from 1517): the overlords' dossiers should carry vassal events naming cholula; this shape stays the city-state's own land.

ledger.note: 300 BC: the first pyramid is raised at Cholula. 'When the pyramid was originally built in 300 BCE'; the city 'grew from a very small village to a regional center between 600 BCE and 700 CE' and dates 'back to at least the 2nd century BC'. The Great Pyramid page gives 'Built: c. 3rd century BC' and dates Building A 'to about 200 BC'. The year is the Cholula page's.

650: Cacaxtla and Xochitécatl rise inside what had been Cholula's hinterland. 'Cacaxtla and Xochitecatl prospered 650–900 CE'; 'After the fall of the nearby city Cholula (c. 650 – 750)'. The year is the start of the page's 650–900; the land is the 10 km core of the cacaxtla dossier, whose capital cell lies inside Cholula's 25 km circle. Mirror: cacaxtla /ledger/0 (found, counterpart cholula).

c. 700: the Gulf Coast Olmeca-Xicallanca take over Cholula and make it their capital. In 'The Tlachihualtepetl phase (CE 700–1200)' 'Cholula was taken over by the Gulf Coast group known as the Olmeca-Xicallanca, who made it their capital'; 'residents abandoned the Great Pyramid in the 8th century' (Great Pyramid page). The Olmeca-Xicalanca page dates them only to 'the epiclassic period (after the seventh century)'. Same city, new rulers: a rename, not a new state.

region.text: 'this part of the Tlaxcala–Puebla valley' (Cacaxtla's 30 km hegemony without the city of Cholula)

ledger.note: c. 650–750: Cholula falls and Cacaxtla becomes 'the hegemonic power in this part of the Tlaxcala–Puebla valley'. The Cacaxtla page: 'the fall of the nearby city Cholula (c. 650 – 750)'. The year is the end of the page's range; the zone is the researcher's. The city of Cholula (10 km) is excluded: it stays Cholula's as the Olmeca-Xicallanca capital.

region.text: 'this part of the Tlaxcala–Puebla valley' (Cacaxtla's 30 km hegemony without the city of Cholula)

ledger.note: c. 900: Cacaxtla's 'ascendancy came to an end around 900 CE and, by 1000, the city had been abandoned'; the pages do not say who took the valley. Cholula, the Olmeca-Xicallanca capital through 1200, is the obvious heir; bridging event at confidence 1. Re-read: the Olmeca-Xicalanca page is silent on the end of Cacaxtla and on any successor (it has only 'They crossed mountains and volcanos to settle in Cuernavaca, Chalco and Cholula' and 'dominated parts of central Mexico during the epiclassic period (after the seventh century)'); the Cacaxtla page says 'Its ascendancy came to an end around 900 CE and, by 1000, the city had been abandoned' and, undated, 'Warriors from Cacaxtla appear to have taken over Cholula for a time, but they were ultimately expelled by the Toltecs'. Still an inference at confidence 1.

1200: the Tolteca-Chichimeca conquer Cholula. 'In CE 1200, ethnic Tolteca-Chichimeca conquered Cholula'; the Great Pyramid page puts the 'Toltec-Chichimeca conquest of the city in the twelfth century'. The city continues under new rulers.

region.text: the city, 'peacefully transferred to Spanish hands'

ledger.note: 1521: Cholula passes to Spain. After the Spanish–Aztec war Cholula 'was peacefully transferred to Spanish hands'; 'In 1519, the Tlaxcalans led Cortés and his troops to Cholula' (the massacre); 'In 1517, Cholula seceded from the Tlaxcala Triple Alliance, opting to join the far more powerful Aztec equivalent'. The year is that of the war's end, which the page does not state; confidence 2.

notes: Added at the orchestrator's request (Cliopatria lacks Cholula). The dossier runs to 1521 because the city-state lived on past this group's 900 cut-off; the Postclassic events (Tolteca-Chichimeca 1200, subjection to Tlaxcala 'sometime between 1200 and 1517', the Aztec alliance of 1517, the massacre of 1519) should be checked by the Postclassic Mesoamerica group, and Tlaxcala (no Cliopatria row) and aztec-triple-alliance should carry vassal_start events naming cholula. Disagreements: the Cholula page dates the first pyramid to 300 BCE and the growth period to 600 BCE–700 CE; the Great Pyramid page gives the 3rd century BC and Building A c. 200 BC. The Cacaxtla page's 'fall of Cholula (c. 650–750)' and the Cholula page's Olmeca-Xicallanca capital (700–1200) are reconciled as a change of rulers (rename, 700) plus the loss of the northern valley to Cacaxtla (750). Wikidata id unknown (wikidata.org unreachable). Pages opened: 4 of a budget of 2–5 (Olmeca-Xicalanca thin). REPAIR 2026-10-18 (reviewer's fail): (1) the -300..749 keyframe now ends in 649; the new keyframe cholula_650 (650..749) is the 25 km circle minus Cacaxtla's 10 km core, with a 650 loss (counterpart cacaxtla, confidence 2, Cacaxtla page 'prospered 650–900 CE') and cacaxtla /ledger/0 now names cholula as its counterpart. (2) The Teotihuacan overlap is resolved in the teotihuacan dossier (its shapes are redrawn as a 40 km circle around the city and share no cell with Cholula); no page makes Cholula a Teotihuacan dependency, so no vassal events were added in either dossier. (3) Extra correction found on the way, not in the review: the 750..900 shape (Cholula 25 km minus Cacaxtla 30 km) left the city's own cell outside, so the 10 km city circle is added back and the 750 loss, the 900 gain and Cacaxtla's 30 km land (cacaxtla dossier, keyframe 750, events 750 and 900, successor land) exclude it. (4) NOT applied, with the reason: vassal events for Tlaxcala ('Sometime between 1200 and 1517, Cholula was conquered by the neighboring city-state of Tlaxcala') and for the 1517 secession to the Aztec alliance are not written into this ledger. The schema makes 'counterpart' the vassal itself in vassal_start and vassal_end, so the event sits in the overlord's ledger and names cholula as the vassal, and window-brief rule 4 turns a vassal_start into 'status vassal with suzerain = this slug': written here with counterpart tlaxcala it would make Cholula the suzerain of Tlaxcala. The page also gives no year for the Tlaxcala conquest, only a range. The events belong in tlaxcala and aztec-triple-alliance (am-03) naming cholula; tlaxcala is listed as a counterpart needing a dossier. (5) The 900 regain of the valley stays an inference at confidence 1: the Olmeca-Xicalanca page (re-read) is silent and the Cacaxtla page names no heir. Residual approximation: after 900 the Cacaxtla ring (9 cells) is wider than Cholula's 25 km circle (only 3 of its cells fall inside it), so the other 6 are nobody's land in the keyframes.
